sections.title: WHEN IS AN SMP TREATMENT UNSUCCESSFUL?
bullets: Too large dots – blurred and unnatural
Bluish or grayish-green tones
Unnatural hairline – too high, too low, or perfectly straight
Uneven density and patchy result
Pigment has spread, migrated, or darkened
Lack of experience of the practitioner
Poor or no formal training
Work done without understanding scalp anatomy and facial aesthetics
Use of wrong tools and methods
text: The most common issues we see:
In over 90% of cases, the cause is:
SMP is not a regular tattoo. It requires precise technique, an eye for detail, and experience.
The practitioner’s experience makes the difference between a natural result and one you want to hide.
That’s why at Micro Hair Clinic we offer professional SMP training alongside corrections.
The industry needs more knowledge – and fewer rushed, unprofessional jobs.

In such cases, we do not perform corrections.
Instead, we recommend laser pigment removal in collaboration with reliable, certified centers.
Our goal is not to 'cover up' the problem at any cost but to provide a solution that truly looks natural.
If this is not possible – we will tell you honestly.
Sometimes pigment removal is the only path to a lasting solution.
Consider correction if:

list.q: Is a bad SMP always fixable?
list.a: Not always – but most can be improved. Assessment is free and honest.

list.q: Do I need to remove pigment with a laser first?
list.a: In some cases yes. In others, correction is possible immediately.

list.q: How quickly can I get a session?
list.a: If the SMP is older than a few weeks – often immediately. Fresh treatments are best evaluated after stabilization.

list.q: Is it possible to get a new hairline?
list.a: Yes – if skin condition and pigment placement allow it.
